narrative.overview: RotorBench should feel like a well-organized workbench for planning, assembling, and reviewing an FPV aircraft. Instrument panels, compact measurements, and explicit state labels carry the personality.
keyCharacteristics: Matte flight-bench surfaces and signal-lime actions
Archivo for interface voice and IBM Plex Mono for measurements
Compact instrument panels, clear sections, and explicit safety boundaries
Responsive workbench layouts rather than a fixed phone shell

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime marks action or active state; it is not a decorative accent for every card.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace is used when the content is data, a command, or a measured value, not as a generic technical costume.

rules.name: The One-Elevation Rule
rules.body: A surface declares depth with either a border or a shadow system appropriate to its role; avoid ghost-card combinations that add both without meaning.

dos: Do keep planning, imported evidence, live observation, and hardware verification visibly distinct.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for measurements, commands, IDs, and parser facts.
Do retain 44px controls and test 390px and 1440px layouts.
Do use quiet borders and tonal surfaces before adding shadows.
donts: Don't turn every section into an identical rounded card.
Don't use lime as a broad decorative wash.
Don't present estimated or imported data as manufacturer-verified or hardware-ready.
Don't hide missing compatibility with a green badge.
Don't use color without a text label or icon-equivalent cue.
